title: What REALLY Happens If You Swallow Chewing Gum?
sources: Mayo Clinic, What happens to swallowed gum
American Academy of Pediatrics, Gastrointestinal bezoars

lines.text: You've probably been told that swallowed gum sits inside your stomach for seven years.
lines.caps: Does gum stay in | your *stomach | for *7 years?

lines.text: The truth is, that is completely false.
While your stomach acid can't dissolve the rubbery synthetic gum base, your body breaks down everything else.
lines.caps: Stomach acid breaks | down the *sugars | and *flavoring

lines.text: Powerful muscular contractions called peristalsis push the gum through your intestines.
Within forty-eight hours, the gum passes out in the toilet completely harmlessly.
However, swallowing huge clumps of gum at once can form a dangerous digestive blockage called a bezoar.
So while an accidental swallow won't hurt, it's always best to spit it out.
lines.caps: One piece is *fine | but always *spit it out!
